title: Be Holy Because I Am Holy

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The LORD said to Moses, "Speak to the entire assembly of Israel and say to them: 'Be holy because I, the LORD your God, am holy.'" - Lev 19:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Speak to the entire assembly. Not just the priests this time — everyone. Farmers, mothers, shepherds, children. And the command given to all of them is the highest one imaginable: be holy, because I am holy.

That should stop us. God does not set the standard at "be decent" or "be better than your neighbours." He sets it at Himself.

But notice the word because. Holiness is not a target we invent or a level we reach by effort. It is a response to who God is. We are to be holy because He is — the way a child picks up the manner of a parent they love.

Notice also what comes next in this chapter. God immediately starts talking about harvests, wages, gossip, and how you treat the deaf. Holiness is not floating above ordinary life. It is exactly there, in the field and the marketplace and the family home.

Peter quotes this verse directly to ordinary Christians: But just as he who called you is holy, so be holy in all you do (1 Pet 1:15-16). In all you do. Not in your religious activities. In everything.

The bar is impossibly high. Which is why we need both a Saviour who met it for us and a Spirit who works it in us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you think of holiness as religious activity, or as ordinary life done rightly?
2. What does it mean that God sets the standard at His own character?
3. Where in your everyday life is God calling you to be holy this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are holy and You call me to reflect You. I cannot do this on my own — work Your holiness into my ordinary days by Your Spirit. Amen.
